html:
Camp Lemonnier, a former French Foreign Legion camp beside Djibouti's airport, has been the main United States military base in Africa since 2002.

After the attacks of September 2001, the United States used it to watch over the Gulf of Aden, Yemen and Somalia, and later to fly drones. France had long kept its own garrison. Japan opened its first overseas base since the Second World War there in 2011, and in 2017 China opened its first overseas military base nearby, close to the Doraleh port.

Rents from the bases bring in a large share of state income. They show the worth of Djibouti's place on the Bab el Mandeb strait, through which a large share of world shipping passes on the way to the Suez Canal.
sum: Camp Lemonnier, a former French Foreign Legion camp beside Djibouti's airport, has been the main United States military base in Africa since 2002.
